name: Judah
overview: Judah, a son of Jacob, emerges in Scripture as a pivotal figure among his brothers, notably intervening to spare Joseph's life by suggesting they sell him to the Ishmaelites rather than kill him. His personal life is marked by complex events, including taking two wives and living at Chezib, where his son Shelah was born. Despite moments of moral failure, Judah's story is foundational, foreshadowing his tribe's leadership role and his significance as an ancestor of Jesus.
